lines.text: אזל 29 אזק
תֵּאזְלִי Jer. 2, 36; prob. to roll, to roll
together; hence
1. to spin, from the rolling or twist-
ing of the thread. So Talmud. אָזַל,
whence אַזְלָאָה weaver, Arab. غزل Conj.
I, IV, غَزْلٌ something spun, Syr. and
Chald. ܥܙܰܠ, עֲזַל, id. comp. kindr. נָזַל to
spin, to flow, both from the idea of rolling.
See Pual.
2. Intrans. to roll off, i. e. to go away,
to depart, espec. quickly, suddenly;
comp. Germ. sich trollen, Engl. to troll,
Gr. νέω to spin, and Mid. νέομαι to go
away, to flee. So in Chald. and Syr.
Comp. Arab. عزل to put away, to re-
move.—Prov. 20, 14 where c. dat. pleon.
לוֹ, like הָלַךְ לוֹ. Jer. 2, 36. Metaph.
to be gone, to fail, as water Job 14, 11;
food 1 Sam. 9, 7; power Deut. 32, 36.
Pual Part. מְאוּזָל something spun,
thread, yarn, Ez. 27, 19.
Deriv. אָזֵל.
אֲזַל Chald. i. q. Heb. no. 2. 1. to go
away, to depart, Dan. 6, 19. So also in
Syr. and Samar.
2. to go any where, to take a journey,
אֶזֶל departure, see in אֶבֶן no. 6. b.
* I. אָזַן in Kal not used, pr. accord-
ing to the probable conjecture of Simo-
nis, to be sharp, acute, pointed; whence
אֹזֶן the ear, (which espec. in animals
might be so called from its pointed
shape,) and אָזֵן, אֲזֵנִים arms, pointed
weapons. Comp. ἀκοή, ἀκούω, and ἀκή,
acies, acuo. Kindr. is perh. עָצַן q. v.
Hiph. הֶאֱזִין denom. from אֹזֶן, q. d. to
make ears, i. e. to point or prick up the
ears, ἐνωτίζεσθαι, a Greek word peculiar
to the Sept. version, Arab. أَذَّنَ id.
Hence, to give ear, to hear, to listen, ab-
sol. Is. 1, 2; c. accus. Gen. 4, 23. Job 33,
1; לְ Job 34, 2; אֶל Ps. 77, 2; עַל Prov.
17, 4; עַד Num. 23, 18, both of person
and thing. Spec. of God, to hear and
9, 16; of men, to hear and obey, c. dat.
Neh. 9, 30. Ex. 15, 26.—Fut. 1 pers. אָזִין
for אַאֲזִין Job 32, 11; Part. מֵזִין for מַאֲזִין
Prov. 17, 4.
Deriv. see in Kal, and the four after אֹזֶן.
* II. אָזַן, i. q. Arab. وَزَنَ, to weigh,
to poise; whence מֹאזְנַיִם balances.—
Found only in
Piel. אִזֵּן to weigh, trop. to ponder, to
consider, Ecc. 12, 9, where it is fol-
lowed by synon. חִקֵּר. Rabbin. אִזֵּן to
be weighed, proved.
אָזֵן m. (r. אָזַן I) furniture, implement,
pr. weapon, arms, comp. Chald. אֲזַנִין
arms, and see r. אָזַן I. Deut. 23, 14 and
thou shalt have a little spade עַל אֲזֵנֶךָ
among thy furniture; where many Mss.
read עַל אֲזֵנֶיךָ among thy implements,
which is preferable.—The same sense
of both utensil and weapon exists in
the word כְּלִי.
אֹזֶן f. dual אָזְנַיִם (used also for plur.)
constr. אָזְנֵי, the ear, from r. אָזַן I.
So דִּבֶּר בְּאָזְנֵי פְּלֹנִי to speak in the ears
Arab. أُذْنٌ, أُذُنٌ, Ethiop. እዝን,
Chald. אוּדֶן, אוּדְנָא, contr. אוּנָא; Syr.
ܐܶܕܢܳܐ, ܐܽܘܕܢܳܐ. Comp. Gr. οὖς, Lat. audio.—
Ex. 29, 20. Lev. 8, 23. al. Phrases of
which this word makes part, see under
the verbs גִּלָּה, נָטָה Hiph. פָּתַח, כָּרָה.
of any one, i. e. before any one, in his
presence and hearing, Gen. 20, 8. 23,
יְהוָֹה in mine ears (said) Jehovah, comp.
22, 14. שׂוּם בְּאָזְנֵי פ׳ to put or lay up in
the ears of any one, i. e. to rehearse so
that one may hear with the ear and
lay up in his mind, Ex. 17, 14. שָׁמַע
בְּאָזְנָיו to hear with one’s ears, emphat.
אֻזֵּן שֶׁאֱרָה (ear of Sherah, or She-
rah’s corner) Uzzen-Sherah, pr. n. of
a small city founded by Sherah the
daughter of Ephraim, 1 Chr. 7, 24.
אַזְנוֹת־תָּבוֹר (pr. ears i. e. summits of
Tabor) Aznoth-Tabor, pr. n. of a city in
Naphtali, Josh. 19, 34.
אָזְנִי (auritus) Ozni, pr. n. m. of a son
of the patriarch Gad, Num. 26, 16.
אֲזַנְיָה (whom Jehovah hears) pr. n.
m. Azaniah, Neh. 10, 10.
אֲזִקִּים m. plur. (r. זָנַק) manacles,
chains for the hands, Jer. 40, 1. 4; i. q.
זִקִּים with Aleph prosthetic, which some
Mss. omit in v. 1.

line_status.note: The first letter is a tav with a dagesh dot inside and tsere beneath (the Kethib תֵּאזְלִי of Jer. 2:36), not a he; the alef carries no qamets, and the shewa sits under the zayin. Reading B matches the print exactly.
The Arabic word carries a visible nominative tanwīn (ٌ) above the lām in addition to fatḥa on ghayn and sukūn on zāy; Reading A omits it.

The Syriac word's first (rightmost) letter is Serto ʿe (ܥ), not gamal, matching the Hebrew cognate עזל; and a vowel point (pthaha) is clearly printed above the word, which Reading B omits. Reading A is correct.
Only one interior dot is printed in the middle of the word — the shureq in the vav; the zayin shows no dagesh, so Reading B's מְאוּזָּל adds a dot that isn't on the page.
Under the zayin the print shows two horizontal dots (tsere), not a single bar (patah); the aleph carries qamets, and the closing period is spaced off from the word, exactly as in Reading B.

Under the aleph the print shows three dots in a triangle (segol), not the two dots plus patah of hateph-patah; zayin likewise carries segol. So אֶזֶל, matching the lexical form (1 Sam 20:19, אֶבֶן הָאֶזֶל). Rest of the line identical in both readings and confirmed.
Under the zayin the print shows a single horizontal bar (patach), not the two side-by-side dots of tsere; Reading B matches.
